groundings.excerpt:
89: Let \Lambda=\Lambda(x_{1},x_{2},\ldots) be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a {\mathbb{Z}}-linear basis consisting of Schur functions s_{\lambda},
90: where \lambda is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
91: I_{r,n-r}=\mathrm{Span}_{\mathbb{Z}}\left\{s_{\lambda}\mid\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^{r}\right\}
92: of \Lambda. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
93: H^{*}(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}.
94: We will use an overline to denote the projection \Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. Specifically, we will write \overline{\Lambda} as a shorthand for \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. We will also distinguish between s_{\lambda}\in\Lambda, the usual Schur function, and \overline{s}_{\lambda} for its image in \overline{\Lambda}.

claims.text: Theorem 1.2 sets \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and proves that \(J_v\subset\overline\Lambda\) is minimally generated by \(\{\overline{s}_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]

95: We resolve the minimality conjecture [ 12 , Conjecture 4.10] about the basic ideals J_{v}:
96: Theorem 1.2 .
97: Given a bigrassmannian permutation v=v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_{n} let
98: \displaystyle i
99: \displaystyle\coloneqq s-t+1,
100: \displaystyle j
101: \displaystyle\coloneqq r-t+1,
102: \displaystyle a
103: \displaystyle\coloneqq\min(n-r-i,r-j),
104: \displaystyle b
105: \displaystyle\coloneqq\min(i,j).
106: Then the basic ideal J_{v}, thought of as an ideal of H^{*}(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}, is minimally generated by
107: (4)
108: \{\overline{s}_{\mu}\mid i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.
109: That ( 4 ) generates J_{v} is [ 12 , Theorem 4.8] . The conjectural part, which we prove,
110: is the minimality claim, that is, no generator can be removed without changing the ideal.
